what.en: active fire detections by the VIIRS satellite sensor
what.km: ការរកឃើញភ្លើងកំពុងឆេះ ដោយឧបករណ៍ VIIRS លើផ្កាយរណប

definition.en: How many times NASA's VIIRS sensor spotted a vegetation fire burning in a year. It sees smaller fires than the older MODIS count, so its numbers are higher.
definition.km: ចំនួនដងដែលឧបករណ៍ VIIRS របស់ NASA ឃើញភ្លើងឆេះរុក្ខជាតិក្នុងមួយឆ្នាំ។ វាឃើញភ្លើងតូចៗជាងការរាប់ MODIS ចាស់ ដូច្នេះចំនួនរបស់វាខ្ពស់ជាង។

en: Each detection is a 375 m patch with a fire in it when the satellite passed, about twice a day. A big fire seen on many days counts many times.
Cloud and thick smoke hide fires, so a cloudy year can show fewer.
The record starts in 2013, so it is shorter than the MODIS fire count.
km: ការរកឃើញនីមួយៗ គឺជាផ្ទៃ 375 ម៉ែត្រដែលមានភ្លើង នៅពេលផ្កាយរណបឆ្លងកាត់ ប្រហែលពីរដងក្នុងមួយថ្ងៃ។ ភ្លើងធំដែលឃើញច្រើនថ្ងៃ ត្រូវរាប់ច្រើនដង។

what.km: សន្ទស្សន៍អាកាសធាតុភ្លើង (FWI) មធ្យមប្រចាំឆ្នាំ

definition.en: How easily the weather lets a fire start and spread, from heat, dry air, wind and days without rain, averaged over the year. It rates the weather, not fires that actually burned. A value of 10 or more counts as high fire danger.
definition.km: កម្រិតដែលអាកាសធាតុធ្វើឱ្យភ្លើងងាយឆេះ និងរាលដាល ដោយផ្អែកលើកម្តៅ ខ្យល់ស្ងួត ខ្យល់បក់ និងចំនួនថ្ងៃគ្មានភ្លៀង យកជាមធ្យមក្នុងមួយឆ្នាំ។ វាវាយតម្លៃអាកាសធាតុ មិនមែនភ្លើងដែលបានឆេះពិតប្រាកដទេ។ តម្លៃ 10 ឬលើសនេះ ចាត់ទុកថាគ្រោះថ្នាក់ភ្លើងខ្ពស់។

en: Worked out from a weather model steered by observations, not measured at a weather station.
The index was made for Canadian forests. The same value can mean more or less danger in other landscapes.
Bare desert, ice and water are left out. Snowy winter months count as no danger.

វាលខ្សាច់ទទេ ទឹកកក និងទឹក មិនត្រូវបានរាប់បញ្ចូលទេ។ ខែរដូវរងាដែលមានព្រិល ចាត់ទុកថាគ្មានគ្រោះថ្នាក់។

notes: fire_viirs: VIIRS S-NPP 375 m detections from the FIRMS yearly country zips (viirs-snpp_<YEAR>_all_countries.zip). Every row carries version '2' = standard processing (Collection 2, VNP14IMG), not NRT ('2.0NRT'); so the dataset DOI is the standard product 10.5067/VIIRS/VNP14IMG.002, not the NRT 10.5067/FIRMS/VIIRS/VNP14IMGT_NRT.002 (that DOI resolves but names the NRT stream we do not use). Counted: type 0 (presumed vegetation fire) with confidence 'n' or 'h' ('l' dropped), matching MODIS `fire` (type 0, confidence >= 30). Cell = sum of detections whose lat/lon fall in it (count, store sum true). The FIRMS country files cover land detections assigned to a country; offshore type-3 rows are excluded anyway. First year 2013, not 2012: S-NPP VIIRS detections begin 20 Jan 2012 (the 2012 zip's earliest rows are 2012-01-21), so 2012 misses ~3 weeks of the N-hemisphere tropical dry season and is left NaN. Cells whose 2013-2024 mean is below MIN_MEAN = 3 fires/yr are NaN in every year (same rule as data/fire_years.f32 for MODIS). VIIRS sees far more small fires than MODIS (roughly 5-10x the counts), so fire_viirs and fire are not comparable in level, only in trend. fire_weather: GFWED v2.0, fwiCalcs.MERRA2/Default/MERRA2.CORRECTED (MERRA-2 T, RH, wind, snow with MERRA-2 gauge-corrected precipitation PRECTOTCORR; all NASA). Yearly value = day-weighted mean of the 12 monthly-mean FWI files, not days above a danger class: the daily route is 8,766 files (5.4 GB even reading only the FWI field by byte range) and NCCS served ~0.2 MB/s here, i.e. ~8 h; monthly is 288 range reads, 170 MB. A month with no FWI at a pixel (snow shutdown) counts as 0; a pixel with no FWI in any month (GFWED veg mask: water, bare, ice, land fraction < 0.1) is NaN, so the grid is land only. The definition text names FWI >= 10 as the start of the 'high' class (Canadian CWFIS classes: low 0-5, moderate 5-10, high 10-20, very high 20-30, extreme 30+); the GFWED site stresses classes need local calibration, so no threshold is applied to the data. Native 0.5 x 0.625 deg pixels averaged to 1 deg with build_catalog.bin1. The `gfwed` dataset record has no DOI (none exists); the method DOI is on `gfwed-paper`. fire_weather also cites the existing `merra2-paper`. fire.py reads only the FWI variable from each netCDF-3 file via HTTP Range (parses the header for its offset). Downloads use only *.nasa.gov hosts (firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov, portal.nccs.nasa.gov); no Earthdata login needed for either. Cache: tools/cache/fire/ keeps the FIRMS zips (~4.4 GB) and per-year count .npy, and gfwed/*.f4 monthly FWI fields (170 MB). Nothing extra to install.
